notes: Account intro: engaged via solutions webinar (Nov 2025). CTO Marcus Hsu pushed for on-prem-like guarantees for real-time personalization stack.
Qualification: strong need for reserved capacity, predictable throughput for peak shopping events, strict audit/logging controls. Very cost-aware but willing to commit for guarantees.
Quote from CTO: "We need p99 to be predictable under load — bursts ok, but sustained SLOs must hold. If you can commit to throughput, budget follows."
POC scope agreed: Dedicated POC (4-week) -> load testing, soak testing, representative prompt suite, failure/fallback scenarios, SLA language draft.
POC timeline (high level): kickoff 2026-02-18, initial provisioning 02-20, baseline load tests 02-22 to 02-24, 72h soak 02-25 to 02-28, canary traffic run 03-02, SLA review 03-04, exec review 03-05.
Provisioning notes: Redwood provisioned 4x A100-80GB equivalent for POC (customer requested H100 for production). Customer will evaluate reserved 8-12 GPU pool for initial commit.

Representative prompts used for tests: short-chat (avg 60 tokens), search-rerank (avg 130 tokens), personalization-merge (avg 350 tokens). We captured token length distribution and tail latencies per workload.
Load test summary: peak test sim = 1,500 rps (short-chat mix), sustained 30m windows at 800 rps achieved with 4x A100 equiv. Observed avg latency p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=320ms for short-chat path.

Soak test summary (72h): sustained mixed-workload 300 rps with 20% bursts. Memory/KV cache warm-up improved throughput by ~18% across runs. No OOMs. 3 transient 503s during a manual cluster restart — auto-fallback routing worked as expected.

Throughput guarantees discussion: Redwood proposes baseline reserved throughput per GPU = ~400 requests/sec (short-chat mix). Customer asks for contractual 95% of baseline during sustained windows and credits for missed SLOs.

Latency SLO proposal: target p99 <= 350ms for short-chat at 95% of committed throughput. Customer requested tighter p99 <= 300ms for 50% of traffic during business hours (asked as optional burst SLA). Legal wants SLO credit tiers mapped to incident windows.

Cost modeling: POC cost run-rate shows committed reserved pool (8x H100) approx 55% lower unit cost vs on-demand Dedicated for their traffic profile when combined with caching/batching from Optimize suggestions.

Routing/fallback: tested automatic fallback to smaller model variant (quantized 13B) during simulated capacity pressure. Quality delta measured via A/B eval on 150 prompts: acceptability drop ~4% but within customer's threshold for non-core flows.

Security/compliance: SSO/SAML validated in staging. Audit log capture hooked into their Splunk instance (sample events in drive doc). KMS integration demoed; asked for HSM-backed key option for production.

Open questions from customer: 1) formal SLA language and credit calculations, 2) exact mapping of reserved GPU counts to their peak traffic days, 3) support & on-call escalation matrix for production.

poc_details: Objective: prove Dedicated can meet latency SLOs and throughput guarantees for real-time personalization use-case at peak + sustained traffic
Test harness: k6 and JMeter hybrid + in-house replay of production traces anonymized (sample size ~50k requests)
Workload mixes: short-chat 50%, rerank 20%, embeddings batch 10%, long-personalization 20%
Representative prompts: 150 short-chat templates, 80 rerank queries, 30 long-personalization examples (avg 350 tokens)
Key metrics captured: requests/sec, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, KV-cache hit rate, error rates, cost per 1M tokens
Results summary: baseline model (fp16) on 4x GPUs: sustained mixed throughput 300 rps, tokens/sec ~18k, p99 overall 380ms; optimized config with q4 and cache: tokens/sec +22%, p99 reduced to 320ms
Failure scenarios executed: node restart, network partition (VPC tier), sudden 3x traffic spike — measured graceful fallback and degraded QoS rather than hard failures
Recommendation from SE: reserve 8 H100 equiv for initial production with autoscale headroom of +50% burst, include 24/7 on-call for first 90 days, and enable cache pinning for personalization keys
